hints: The total sum is n(n+1)/2; it must be even.
If divisible by 4, pairs from the ends can be grouped to give each set the same sum.
If the total is 2 mod 4, a constructive alternating pattern works; output each number exactly once.
analogy: You are balancing a numbered pile; first check whether the total weight can be split evenly, then build groups that meet at half.
example: For n=7, total 28. Sets {1,2,4,7} and {3,5,6} each total 14.
algorithm: Reject when n(n+1)/2 is odd. Otherwise construct by processing blocks of four: when n mod 4 is 0, assign two smallest and two largest in each block to one side; when n mod 4 is 3, seed the groups with {1,2} and {3}, then use four-number blocks. Print sizes and elements.
correctness: Equal-sum sets require an even total; the construction assigns each block equal weight, with the seed handling the n mod 4 = 3 case.
complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space if storing both sets (or O(1) auxiliary space when streaming).
